newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav June wages rise 9.9 pct to 807 dinars.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav June wages rise 9.9 pct to 807 dinars.

text.p: The Federal Statistics Office reported the following economic indicator details.
YUGOSLAV AVERAGE NET WAGES JUNE MAY JUNE 96
NOTES -- June wages were 52.3 percent up in nominal terms and 24.9 percent up in real terms against the same month 1996.
Compared to December 1996, June wages were 14.9 percent higher in nominal terms and 10.1 percent higher in real terms.
Cumulative January-June wages rose 53.9 percent against the same six-month period last year, and 31.6 percent against the average for 1996.

The Federal Statistics Office revised its methodology of calculating average wages in January 1997 to include all employed who worked in a given month, regardless of whether they all received wages earned in that month.
Data do not include private sector. Data cover Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
